clues: A river cuts this big town in two as it flows from west to east. The town spreads wide in the heart of its state.
Summers here are hot and humid, and winters are cool. Droughts can drag on, then heavy rain can flood the streets.
By 1907, this fast town had grown past the old seat of the land. Soon after, the capital was moved here for good.
This town was born in just one day, the Land Run of 1889. Folks raced in to claim land, and a town rose in hours.
The state governor works in this place, the largest in the state. Lawmakers meet here in the state capitol.
